2. The relevant facts of the case are that the petitioner filed the above Misc. Case for pre-emption of the case land under Section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The case was dismissed for default on 3.3.83 in presence of the opposite parties, as the petitioner did not take any step for preemptory hearing of the case. The petitioner then preferred the above appeal against that order of dismissal. The learned Subordinate Judge dismissed the appeal holding that the appeal is not maintainable by making the following observation. 

 2. Mr. Mansur Habib, the learned Advocate for the petitioner has taken me through the impugned orders of the courts below. He contends that the learned Subordinate Judge has committed an error of law in holding that the appeal against the order of dismissal of a case under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, is not maintainable, in view of the clear provision of appeal laid down in Section 96(12) of aforesaid Act. Section 96(12) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act runs as follows :- 

 3. The contention of the learned Advocate is correct. It appears that the learned Subordinate Judge is not aware of this special provision of Appeal made in section 96(12) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The order of the learned Subordinate Judge, is therefore, illegal, and he has committed an error of law in dismissing the appeal only on the ground that it is not maintainable. The learned Subordinate Judge did not consider the appeal on merit.
